::: {.learner-hero}
Learner hub for University of Utah Internal Medicine residents preparing to lead Code Blue and Rapid Response teams. Use this site before, during, and after the in-person session.

The goal is not to memorize every algorithm; it is to practice the first decisions that make resident-led emergencies safer.
:::

## Start Here

::: {.hub-grid}
::: {.hub-card}
### Before the Session

- Review the four micro-skill modules.
- Bring questions from real code/RRT experiences.
- Complete the pre-session survey when the 2026 link is released.

**Survey status:** 2026 link TBD.
:::

::: {.hub-card}
### During the Session

- Practice taking explicit leadership.
- Interpret shockable and non-shockable rhythms out loud.
- Escalate resources early when the room is not safe enough.
- Run hands-on Zoll and scenario practice.
:::

::: {.hub-card}
### After the Session

- Bookmark the resources page.
- Revisit the case rhythm strips.
- Send near-misses, big wins, or unclear workflows to the CMRs so this course stays current.

**Post-session survey:** 2026 link TBD.
:::
:::

## Learning Objectives

By the end of the session, learners should be able to:

- Assume and communicate team leadership immediately on arrival.
- Identify VF/VT on the monitor and deliver shocks when warranted.
- Escalate care and marshal resources appropriately.
- Operate the Zoll R-Series defibrillator safely and efficiently.
- Conclude the event, hand off the patient, and set up a debrief.

::: {.callout-tip}
Didactics alone have limits. Regular review, simulation, and feedback after real events are what turn these skills into reflexes.
:::

## Why This Course Exists

Stakeholders from Code Blue and Rapid Response teams, including senior residents, nurses, respiratory therapists, and quality leads, identified three recurring hazards during resident-led responses:

1. Unclear team leadership, which can cause role confusion, low psychological safety, and decreased collaboration. [@steinbach_effective_2024]
2. Failure to cardiovert or defibrillate shockable rhythms.
3. Delayed critical decisions, including calling for help, initial stabilization, and transport to ICU.

This seminar targets those hazards through brief micro-skills, discussion, and hands-on scenarios.
